newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA SAYS 88 PCT OF FOREIGN DEBT IS LONG-TERM.
newsitem.headline: CHINA SAYS 88 PCT OF FOREIGN DEBT IS LONG-TERM.

text.p: China's foreign debt stands at about $120 billion and of that 88 percent is in the form of long-term loans, central bank governor Dai Xianglong told a news conference on Thursday.
He gave no breakdown of the currencies in which China holds its foreign debt.

At end-June last year, China's debt composition included $98 billion as mid- and long-term debt, or 89.4 percent of the total, compared with 88.8 percent in the period the year before, state media have said. Short-term at end-June, 1996, was about $11.6 billion.
China's debt service ratio in 1995 was about 7.3 percent, well within the recognised safety level of 20 percent, officials have said.
Economists say that given China's cautious approach to its foreign debt, that ratio is unlikely to have changed substantially.
